title: Authentication Token Acceptance via URL Query Parameters Leaks Session Credentials
description: The authentication middleware accepts credentials via the URL query string parameter req.query.token. Query parameter tokens are automatically logged in web server access logs, reverse proxy logs, browser histories, and outgoing HTTP Referer headers, exposing user credentials to unauthorized third parties.
root_cause: server/authMiddleware.ts line 19 extracts authentication tokens from req.query.token alongside standard Authorization headers.
intended_behavior: Authentication credentials must be accepted strictly via the Authorization: Bearer <token> request header or secure HTTP-only cookies, never via URL query parameters.

trace.description: Extracts session token from req.query.token query parameter.
Authenticates caller using query-string token, leaving the secret token in server access logs.

conditions.description: Client or external link provides the auth token as a URL query parameter.

execution.attacker_perspective: Network eavesdropper, log viewer, or downstream referrer observer
instructions: 1. Send HTTP GET to any protected endpoint passing the token in the query string.
2. Verify the server successfully authenticates the request.
3. Inspect server access logs and intermediate proxy logs to observe the token logged in cleartext.
execution.observed_result: The server accepts the query parameter token, successfully authenticates the request, and reflects the token in web server access logs.

remediation.strategy: Remove req.query.token extraction and require the standard Authorization: Bearer <token> HTTP header for all authenticated requests.

likelihood.reason: Requires attacker access to server access logs, reverse proxy logs, browser history, or Referer header destinations.

impact.reason: Exposure of customer session token results in complete account takeover for the affected user.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by explicit source code extraction in server/authMiddleware.ts line 19.

title: Unsigned JWT Fallback Allows Unauthenticated Full ADMIN Takeover
description: When Supabase verification fails or is bypassed, authMiddleware.ts falls back to parsing the raw base64url payload of the token without verifying its cryptographic signature. It assigns the ADMIN role if decoded.role === "service_role", enabling unauthenticated external attackers to forge an unsigned token and obtain unrestricted administrative access to all /api/admin/* endpoints.
root_cause: server/authMiddleware.ts lines 81-127 falls back to decoding the token payload via Buffer.from(parts[1], "base64url") without verifying cryptographic signatures, granting the ADMIN role on decoded.role === "service_role".
intended_behavior: Authentication tokens must be verified cryptographically against the trusted identity provider (Supabase) before any claims are trusted. Invalid or unverified tokens must be rejected immediately.

trace.description: Extracts Authorization Bearer token header from incoming unauthenticated HTTP request.
Decodes unverified base64url payload into JSON without cryptographic signature verification.
Assigns role: "ADMIN" based on untrusted decoded.role === "service_role" claim and stores profile in inMemoryStore.
Grants access to protected /api/admin/* routes because req.user.role is evaluated as ADMIN.

conditions.description: Attacker supplies an HTTP Authorization header with an unsigned two-part token containing role: service_role.

instructions: 1. Craft an unsigned JWT with header {"alg":"none"} and payload {"sub":"admin-exploit","role":"service_role","exp":9999999999}.
2. Send HTTP GET /api/admin/overview with header Authorization: Bearer <crafted-token>.
3. Observe that the server returns HTTP 200 OK with sensitive store overview data, confirming full administrative access.
execution.observed_result: Server assigns req.user with role ADMIN and grants unauthenticated caller access to all administrative store endpoints.

remediation.strategy: Completely eliminate the unverified token parsing fallback in authMiddleware.ts. Reject requests with missing or invalid Supabase signatures.

likelihood.reason: Trivial to construct; requires no existing credentials, network positioning, or timing conditions.

impact.reason: Complete compromise of the store: attacker can initiate Cashfree refunds, modify product prices, toggle store shutdown, and export all customer PII.

confidence.reason: Verified through static code tracing and confirmed locally via authMiddleware execution logic.

title: Cashfree Webhook HMAC Verification Lacks Maximum Clock Skew Bound
description: verifyWebhookSignature in server/services/cashfreeService.ts computes an HMAC over the x-webhook-timestamp and raw body, but does not verify that the timestamp falls within an acceptable time window (e.g. 5 minutes). While paymentPersistenceService maintains event deduplication, a delayed or replayed webhook before initial recording could be processed.
claimed_root_cause: server/services/cashfreeService.ts lines 223-248 verifies HMAC signature integrity but lacks a clock-skew check to reject expired or future-dated webhook timestamps.

trace.description: Receives x-webhook-timestamp and x-webhook-signature headers from incoming webhook.
Constructs HMAC payload as ${timestampHeader}${rawString} without checking timestamp validity window.
Processes payment confirmation state transition based on the verified payload.

blockers: Cashfree production webhook delivery retry timeline and maximum acceptable clock skew require validation against merchant documentation and live gateway behavior.

validation_plan.local: Execute a test script against verifyWebhookSignature with a valid signature but a timestamp from 24 hours ago to confirm signature passes.
validation_plan.deployment: Review Cashfree merchant dashboard webhook delivery logs to inspect actual timestamp deltas during peak traffic.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on Guest Orders Exposes Customer PII
description: GET /api/orders/:orderNumber enforces customer ownership only when order.user_id is present. For guest orders, order.user_id is null/undefined. Consequently, any authenticated customer can request any guest order by order number, revealing the recipient name, unmasked mobile phone number, complete delivery address, ordered items, and payment details without phone verification.
root_cause: server/routes/orderRoutes.ts line 780 checks if (order.user_id && order.user_id !== req.user.id), which evaluates to false for all guest orders where user_id is null or undefined.
intended_behavior: The GET /api/orders/:orderNumber route should deny access to CUSTOMER users if the order belongs to a different customer or if it is a guest order lacking a matching user_id. Guest orders should only be accessible via the dedicated POST /api/orders/guest-status endpoint which requires mobile phone verification.

trace.description: Receives orderNumber from an authenticated CUSTOMER request.
Evaluates if (order.user_id && order.user_id !== req.user.id); for guest orders with null user_id, condition evaluates to false.
Returns the full order object containing customer recipient_name, recipient_phone, and street_address.

conditions.description: Attacker has registered or logged in as an ordinary customer.
Target order was placed as a guest order (user_id is null/undefined).

instructions: 1. Place a guest order as an unauthenticated buyer, generating an order with user_id = null.
2. Log in as a separate customer and send GET /api/orders/<guestOrderNumber> with the customer JWT.
3. Observe HTTP 200 OK with the full unmasked guest recipient name, phone number, and address.
execution.observed_result: Server returns unmasked customer PII and delivery details for third-party guest orders without phone verification.

remediation.strategy: Reject customer access if order.user_id does not equal req.user.id, explicitly denying access to guest orders through the authenticated endpoint.

likelihood.reason: Requires knowing or iterating order numbers, but order numbers follow predictable patterns and any valid customer account qualifies.

impact.reason: Exposes sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (recipient name, unmasked phone number, delivery address) for all guest orders.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated by logic flaw in orderRoutes.ts line 780 and contrasted with secure phone verification in guest-status route.
